question_text: A government employee's gross monthly salary is P30,000. Deductions amount to P7,500. What percentage is deducted?

hint_ladder.title: Find the Right Numbers
hint_ladder.text: This is a 'part of whole' problem. Find the 'part' (the deduction) and the 'whole' (original salary before deductions).

hint_ladder.title: The Simple Percentage Rule
hint_ladder.text: Use the formula: (Part / Whole) x 100. Part is the smaller deducted amount, Whole is the full gross salary.

hint_ladder.title: Plug In Your Numbers
hint_ladder.text: Your Part is P7,500. Your Whole is P30,000. So the calculation is (7,500 / 30,000) x 100.

hint_ladder.title: Do the Math
hint_ladder.text: First, divide 7,500 by 30,000. You get 0.25. Then multiply 0.25 by 100 to get 25%.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you used net pay (P22,500) as the whole, getting 20% instead of using gross salary.

B.text: Correct. You identified the deduction as the part and the gross salary as the whole to get 25%.

C.text: You might have chosen C because you mistakenly used the net pay as the base, giving 33.3%.

D.text: You might have chosen D because a calculation slip like adding or subtracting wrongly gave you 35%.

next_time_rule: Always identify the original 'whole': the amount before deductions. Then use (Part / Whole) x 100.
deconstruct_text:
Imagine you’re a Barangay Treasurer checking your payslip. Gross salary: P30,000. Then you see deductions: P7,500 for taxes, GSIS, PhilHealth. The question: what percentage of your gross is being deducted?

Don’t panic. The formula is simple: divide the part (deduction) by the whole (gross salary) then multiply by 100. (P7,500 / P30,000) x 100 = 25%.

Tandaan: ang 'whole' ay palaging ang original amount before any bawas. Wag gumamit ng net pay as the base — that's a classic trap.

Now you know: whenever HR hands you that payslip, you can quickly compute your deduction rate. Sipag at diskarte, pasado ka!
